tree: Wife of Michael Žubrinić; mother of Nicolaus (b. 24 January 1834)

why: Her baptismal entry is real and hers: Otočac 1835, entry 41, daughter of Marcus Orešković adoptatus Sekula and Lucia née Sekula of Dubrava 29. Six further ancestors hang below this join.

tree: Asserted, with no document — this archive called it Disputed
record: Documented: Senj marriages, 8 December 1920, page 366 entry 41
why: The marriage entry names the groom's parents as Juraj Blažević and Tereza r. Žubrinić, and annotates them mrt. — deceased — which puts Juraj's death before December 1920. He remains undated and unplaced, and nothing yet links him to Toma above.

tree: 14 March 1806
record: 14 March 1806 — confirmed
why: The Vrbnik baptisms for 1806, house 244, read: Die 14. Martii Ao 1806 baptizavi ego Michaël Kombol C.L. infantem lege natum patre Joanne, Matre Marthæ Antich Papa, nomine Josephum. The tree's date is exact. The entry also names his father Joannes (ahnentafel 48) and his mother Martha, and gives the godparents as the village judge Mathias Jellichich and his wife Margarita.

tree: Josephum
record: Josephus — and the priest wrote the accusative himself
why: The register reads nomine Josephum. That is the priest's own Latin, not a modern transcriber's slip: Michaël Kombol writes nomine followed by the accusative in every entry on the page — Mariam, Joannem, Matthæam, Magdalenam, Nicolaum. The tree copied the register faithfully and inherited its grammar.

tree: Gerkacs (Gergacs)
record: Gergacs
why: The Karlobag register for August 1789 reads Mariam natam pridie ex Michaele et Lucia Gergacs. The register's spelling is Gergacs; Gerkacs is the secondary form and the tree carries it first. The entry also gives her mother as Lucia — written over a struck-out name — and her father as Michael.

tree: 11 August 1789
record: August 1789, born the day before baptism — consistent
why: The entry says natam pridie, born the previous day, and sits in the August 1789 sequence after the entry of 9 August. That is consistent with 11 August but the scan does not itself carry a day number; the exact day comes from the index, not the page.

tree: Born 22 April 1777, Karlobag
record: April 1777, Karlobag, born the day before — consistent
why: The Karlobag register reads: baptizavi Infantem heri natum ex Georgio et Maria Uroda Conjugibus hujus Loci, cui impositum est Nomen Joannis Georgij. It confirms the year, the place and both parents, and shows he was born the day before the baptism — but the page carries no day number, so 22 April comes from the index rather than the register. The godparents are Pro-Colonel Joannes Hallinich de Zirfeld and the wife of Captain Daniel de Hofenegg: Military Frontier officers standing for a Karlobag child.

what: She is not this child's mother
tree: Mother of Nicolaus Žubrinić, b. 24 January 1834

Her own 1835 baptism names the same parents the tree gives her and places her at Dubrava N° 29, so she is a real person married here to the wrong man. The join is kept and marked rather than severed, because a wrong join is itself a finding and the only pointer to where the right Maria Orešković should be looked for.

tree: 24 January 1834, Otočac

why: Confiniarius, ex Pago Shumechicza N. 24 — a Military Frontier household at Šumećica house 24. Father Michaël Xubrinich; mother Maria, née Orešković. Godparents Petrus, son of Franciscus Xubrinich, retired Vigiliarum Magister, and Maria, wife of Joannes Xubrinich, Sylvarum Custos at Šumećica.

Either the first wife died and he remarried a second Maria, or there are two men of this name — there are 68 Žubrinić records at Otočac. Nothing read so far chooses between them.

Senj marriages p.348 no.5, her own entry of 1 April 1918, gives 1884 12/5. The register is written from her baptismal certificate; the tree's 17 is five days out. The same entry gives her occupation as nadglednica u tvornici duhana — supervisor in the tobacco factory, not a floor worker — and her parents as Pavao Blažević and Marija r. Tomljanović, poljodjelci iz župe Krmpote.

tree: Michael “Mate” Žubrinić and Maria Catharina Orešković — the same couple as Nicolaus, b. 1834

why: His marriage at Senj on 3 July 1910, where he is kontrolor gradske daće, names his parents as ††Mate Žubrinić i Marija rodj. Orešković, poljodjelci. So both he and Nicolaus (1834) have parents of these names — forty-six years apart. There are two couples of the same two names a generation apart, and the tree has merged them. By date, Maria Catharina (b. 1835) belongs to this later couple, not to the 1834 one.

record: 19 October 1885 — confirmed

tree: 23 October 1888
record: 23 October 1888 — confirmed

tree: 26 July 1907, Senj — no cause, no burial detail

Her husband's death entry of 26 July 1907 calls him udovac iza pok. Tereze — widower of the late Tereza — which is the only real bound anyone has. She was alive in 1884 and dead by July 1907.

tree: Born 1838, Karlobag
record: Baptised 18 September 1838, Karlobag — confirmed
why: Cammeralis nautae Vincentii Pilipich et Matthiae Uroda conjugum hujus Civitatis. The tree renders this as 'finansijski nadmornar. profesional financial arigilia nanta', which is a mangling of the same phrase.

tree: Not recorded

tree: Born 12 January 1779 — the tree's own note adds “(Maybe)”

why: The Karlobag register of 12 January 1779 does record a Caetanus Antonius Bacchi, son of Angelo and Catharina, with a Captain as godfather and the wife of Dominus Georgius Uroda as godmother. But ahn 214's daughter Oliva Andreana died in 1795 and her daughter Oliva Maria Smojver was born 11 March 1781 — two years after this baptism. Two years cannot hold two generations. The right Caetano Bacchi belongs around 1730–1745, and this entry belongs to someone else of the name.

what: Attached on a baptism that is not his son's
tree: Father of Caetano Bacchi
record: Named only in the 1779 entry, which cannot be ahn 214's
why: Angelo and Catharina are in this pedigree solely because the 1779 Karlobag baptism names them as the child's parents. If that baptism belongs to a different Caetano Bacchi, they are that man's parents and not this line's. Nothing else anchors them — Catharina is one of the seven women here with no surname at all.

tree: March 1781, Karlobag
record: Born 11 March 1781 — confirmed
why: Ego Joës Antonius Ivankovich Parochus Loci baptizavi Infantem de 11ma hujus natam ex Vincentio, et Oliva Smoyver, vulgo Vukich, Conjugibus hujus Civitatis, cui impositum est nomen Oliva Maria. The alias Smojver vulgo Vukić is the register's own, and Karlobag is entered as a civitas — a city, not a village.

tree: 11 March 1768, Karlobag
record: Baptised 11 March 1768, born 10 March — confirmed
why: Josephum filium pridie natum a Domino Jacobo et Catharina Pilepich conjugibus hujus loci — pridie, the day before, so born 10 March. The family carries the honorific Dominus. Godparents Dominus Franciscus de Justiniani, a Venetian patrician name, and Domina Ursula, widow of Dominus Joannes Krixich.

tree: Born 12 May 1859, baptised 15 May 1859, Krivi Put 136
record: Confirmed exactly — and the household is entered Confiniarii

Godparents Lucas Tomljanović and Anna Tomljanović, daughter of Andreas. The word Confiniarii makes this a Military Frontier household — so Hedviga descends from Frontier families on the Prpić side as well as the Žubrinić.

tree: Smokvica, Krmpote, Općina Smokvica, Dubrovačko-neretvanska županija

why: Općina Smokvica in Dubrovnik-Neretva county is Smokvica on the island of Korčula, 400 km south. The village meant is Smokvica Krmpotska, inland from Novi Vinodolski, and the tree names it in the same string — Krmpote. This is a geocoder matching the wrong Smokvica, not anybody's claim, which is why it is corrected outright rather than merely noted. It matters: Smokvica kbr. 114 and the parish of sv. Jakov Krmpote are the whole of question 1b.

tree: Senj, Split-Dalmatia, Croatia
record: Senj, Lika-Senj County, Croatia
why: Senj has never been in Split-Dalmatia. It is the seat of its own historic county and sits in Lika-Senj, 200 km north of Split. Another geocoder mismatch. He is the emigrant who reached Port Pirie, so this is the birthplace anyone tracing the Australian branch backwards will search on.

tree: Born 1902, died 1903

An age of one year eight months puts his birth about October 1901 rather than 1902. He died in a scarlet-fever outbreak that killed four people in Senj in eight days — including a second Papić child, from another household, the day before him.

tree: No occupation recorded — her whole event list is born, immigrated, died

why: Remembered in the family and written down in September 2026. Nothing corroborates it, and nothing contradicts it — the tree simply says nothing about her working life at all. The venue is real and datable: the Therapia opened at Crikvenica in 1895 as the Nadvojvoda Josip, was renamed in 1899 when a hydropathic institute was put inside it, and with the Miramare of 1906 is the building that made Crikvenica a health resort. It still stands, renamed Kvarner Palace after an Austrian hotelier bought it in 2013.

What 1948 is in this family is the birth of Ladislava at Crikvenica on 5 March. The crossing therefore happened after April 1953 and before about 1973, and this archive holds nothing at all from inside that span.

record: Register scan held, 2,953 px

tree: Born 4 March 1898, Novi Vinodolski

tree: Born 3 January 1900, Novi Vinodolski
record: Register scan held, 2,953 px

what: A blank house-number column does not mean the household had no number
tree: This archive concluded on 13 September 2026 that “the house number is a village device and it does not reach the town”
record: Novi Vinodolski is a town, and its registers do give house numbers — just not to this family, and not on every page
why: The Senj finding stands as far as Senj goes. But the generalisation drawn from it — that the house number is a village device that does not reach the town — is refuted by four pages of Novi Vinodolski. On str.278 (1894) the column reads 110, 595, —, 313, 647, —, 476, —, —, —, 33, 631; on str.333 (1900) it reads —, 476, 684, 470, —, 223, 629, 103. Towns do record house numbers. On str.293 (1896) and str.314 (1898), by contrast, not one household is numbered at all. So the practice is per register and per priest. Two further things follow. A blank cell is not evidence that a household lacked a number — only that this entry does not record one. And on both pages where numbering happens, Martin Kalanj's household is among the blanks while his neighbours are numbered — which fits a family that came from Klenovica and may never have held a numbered house in Novi. His sister's 1864 baptism, back in the village, is entered Klenovica N° 22 without hesitation.

what: Her gravestone gives the wrong birth date
tree: Born 3 January 1864, Klenovica 22; died 28 May 1936, Crikvenica
record: The Crikvenica stone reads ✻ 19 IX 1863 — the baptismal register reads 3 January 1864
why: The grave at Crikvenica is inscribed ANA DE. FRANCESCHI ✻ 19 IX 1863 ✝ 28 V 1936. The death is exactly right. The birth is not. Her baptism survives: Anno Domini 1864, no. 2 — Anna, legitima, Josephus Kalanj et Rosalia nata Perković ejus uxor, Brinjensis parochiae ruricolae, at Klenovica N° 22, born 3 January 1864 and baptised three days later on 6 January. A register written within the week beats a stone cut after 1936, so the tree's date stands and the stone is the error. Worth saying plainly because the stone is the kind of source that feels conclusive and is not.

what: She is Martin Kalanj's sister, which explains the godparents
tree: Ana Kalanj and Martin Kalanj both children of Josip Kalanj and Rozalija Perković, Klenovica 22
record: Both baptisms name the same parents; and Ana's husband stands godfather to Martin's daughter
why: Ana's 1864 baptism gives her parents as Josephus Kalanj and Rosalia nata Perković at Klenovica 22 — the same couple the tree gives Martin (b. 8 November 1861, Klenovica 22). They are brother and sister. The confirmation arrives from an unexpected direction: at Zora Kalanj's baptism in 1898, Martin's daughter, the godparents are entered as Josip i Ana Defrancesco — that is Ana herself and her husband, the child's aunt and uncle. Four register pages, found loose in a photo library, turn out to document one household across two generations.

what: “Trebinje” is not evidence, and I treated it as though it were
tree: Martin Kalanj, born 8 November 1861 at Klenovica 22; died 5 August 1900 at Trebinje
record: The death has no document behind it at all — its only source is “Geni World Family Tree”, and the place is the bare word “Trebinje” with no country
why:
On 13 September 2026 this archive published his death at Trebinje as an unexplained fact — “a Vinodol man of thirty-eight does not die there by accident… nothing here explains it.” That was too credulous, and the same day's work undermined it.

Look at what the record actually carries. His birth has a full citation — FamilySearch 3QSQ-G99X-KW8J, image 17 of 342, Hrvatski državni arhiv image group 005494765. His death has none: the source is a tree, and the place is one word with no country attached.

And this tree demonstrably moves Lika villages into Bosnia. Michael “Mate” Žubrinić, born 1863 at Prozor near Otočac, is geocoded in this same export to Prozor in the Herzegovina-Neretva Canton — two hundred kilometres away and across a border. That is now the fourth geocoding error documented here.

So the honest position is not that Trebinje needs explaining. It is that Trebinje may not need explaining, because it may not be true — and a death register at Novi Vinodolski or Klenovica would settle it faster than any search in Herzegovina.

what: The Krivi Put status animarum is family material after all
tree: Recorded this morning as “not this family's household — no Pavelić is published here”
record: There are 114 Pavelići in the tree, and Lovro Kalanj married Ana Pavelić
why: The page is tagged to Krešimir Pavelić, and because no Pavelić is published here — this archive publishes nine surname groups and Pavelić is not one — it was set aside as somebody else's household. That was too quick. The tree holds 114 Pavelići, including a Krešimir Pavelić born 3 March 1898, which matches the household head on the page; and Lovro Kalanj married Ana Pavelić. Unpublished is not the same as unrelated, and conflating the two is a failure mode this archive is structurally prone to. The household stays unattached because no published person is named on it; it is no longer described as unconnected.

what: His son's birth year is a typo, and the place proves it
tree: Domianus Perpić died 1888, and his wife Maria Sojath in 1891 — yet their son Georgius Prpić is entered as born 26 March 1962
record: Georgius's own birthplace is given as “Krivi Put 136, Senj, Lika, Austria-Hungary”
why: This was reported here as three separate impossibilities — a child born after his father's death, a child born after his mother's, and a mother of 139. All three are one typing slip. Austria-Hungary ceased to exist in 1918, so nobody was born there in 1962; and Krivi Put 136 is this family's own house, where his parents lived. Everything in the record agrees with 1862 and nothing agrees with 1962. The archive does not edit the tree, so the entry stands as written — but the three contradictions it generated should be read as one, and as solved.

what: Vladimira Baricević cannot be the mother of his children
tree: Joannes Ivan Boras, born 1855, is married to Vladimira Baricević, born 12 December 1907 — a gap of 52 years — and fourteen children hang off her
record: Nine of the fourteen were born before she was, between 1888 and 1906
why: The children are his; the wife is wrong. A woman born in December 1907 did not bear Anđelika in 1888, Draga in 1891, Marija in 1892, Budimir in 1894, Pava and Paulina in 1895, Olga in 1902 or Krešo in 1906 — nor Zdenka in the same year she herself was born. This is the single largest contradiction in the archive and it is one wrong link, not fourteen. Vladimira is a real person attached to the wrong generation, in exactly the shape already documented for Maria Catharina Orešković. Which of Joannes's wives actually bore them is not answerable from this file.

what: Aged 111, and fathered by a label
tree: Gregorius Žubrinić, born 12 March 1785 at Otočac, died 1896 — age 111
record: His children are born 1812–1825, which fits the birth; his recorded father is “Brothers [of Josephus] Žubrinić”
why: The birth date is corroborated by his own children: a man fathering from 1812 to 1825 was born around 1785. It is the death that cannot stand, and the likeliest reading is a grandson of the same name. Worth noting separately because his father's slot holds Brothers [of Josephus] Žubrinić — a sorting label, not a man — which is why he was counted as a joined Žubrinić rather than a loose end until 13 September 2026. The fragments →

what: The same generation is skipped twice in this household
tree: Ten children to Budimir Boras (1894–1954) and Marica Milković (b. 1904), and fourteen to Joannes Ivan Boras (b. 1855) and Vladimira Baricević (b. 1907)
record: Eight of the ten are born 1923–1933; the other two in 1946 and 1960 — the second six years after the father died
why: Read together, the two generations make the same error. Domagoj (1946) and Vladimira (1960) are almost certainly grandchildren attached to their grandparents, and Vladimira Baricević, born 1907, is the right age to have married one of Joannes's sons rather than Joannes himself. If so, Joannes's real wife is missing from the record altogether — and one woman in the wrong slot accounts for eleven of the archive's sixty-three internal contradictions.

what: Her family is from Brinje, not Klenovica — and her own baptism says so
tree: This archive has treated the Kalanji as a Klenovica family throughout — 119 of them are recorded there
record: Her 1864 baptism enters her parents as Brinjensis parochiae ruricolae — country people of the parish of Brinje
why: The line was read, transcribed and then not acted on. Brinje is inland, over the Kapela, some forty kilometres from Klenovica, and the tree independently records her mother Rozalija Perković as being of Brinje. So the Klenovica Kalanji came down to the coast from somewhere else, and every search this archive has run has been on the coast. What forced the re-reading was an American passenger manifest: Stipe Kalanj sailed for New York in 1910 giving his residence as Brinje, and was met by a cousin Juro Borić — and this tree holds a Jure Borić of Brinje whose daughter married a Papić of Senj. Kalanj, Perković and Borić all sit at Brinje. Not one page of the Brinje register has ever been opened, and Brinje appears nowhere in this archive's gazetteer.

what: He emigrated to New York in 1911 — the tree simply stopped
tree: Matthaus (Mate) Žubrinić, born 29 December 1867 at Prozor 50, son of Michael Žubrinić and Marija Rogić. No death, no emigration, nothing after his birth
record: New York passenger list, 1911: Mate Zubrinic, aged 43, residence “Prozon”, sailed on the Saint Louis from Southampton
why: Found on FindMyPast during a two-day trial, 13 September 2026. The manifest gives his residence as Prozor, his age as 43 — which a man born 29 December 1867 is through most of 1911 — his nationality as Croatian, and the wife he left behind as Roza. Surname, village, age and year all agree, and Prozor is a very small place: this archive knows eleven Žubrinići there, all in houses 46 and 50. He was met in New York by his nephew, Stipan Kostelac — and Kostelac marries into this Žubrinić household six times. The tree does hold a Stipan Kostelac married to a Bare Žubrinić, but that man has children born in 1849 and would be ninety in 1911; the New York Stipan is far more likely a grandson of the same name. Nothing in the tree has been edited. This is recorded as what a document says about a man whose record here previously ended at his birth.

what: He is entered as a father at sixteen, and the mother at fifteen
tree: Anton Kljapo Blažević, born 2 May 1824; his son Anton Martin “Tone” Blažević born 1840
record: The mother, Marija Šojat, is born 13 March 1825 — so she is fifteen and he is sixteen at the birth
why: Neither age is impossible and both together are uncommon enough to record. This is a new severity-3 band added on 13 September 2026 for parents aged thirteen to sixteen, raised because George Untersinger fathering at fifteen sat just under the old threshold of thirteen and went unflagged entirely. Two readings fit and this archive cannot choose between them: a couple who married very young — which the Krivi Put registers would show as ordinary or not — or a birth year for the son that is wrong by a few years. The marriage entry would settle it.

tree: Stane Blažević, born 1860; the child Luce born 1876
record: Sixteen years between them
why: Flagged under the band added on 13 September 2026 for parents aged thirteen to sixteen. Both years are bare — no day, no month, no source — so the gap may be an artefact of two estimates rather than a fact about anybody. Recorded rather than resolved.

tree: Wife of Joannes «Ivan» Boras (1855–1926); mother of all fourteen of his children, born 1888–1930
record: Born 12 December 1907 — nineteen years after the eldest of those children
why: She cannot be the mother of children born 1888–1906, and the tree gives Ivan Boras no other wife. One spouse slot is carrying more than one woman. The tell is in the list itself: Zdenka Boras is born 12 December 1907, the same day as Vladimira, so a daughter's birth date has been copied into the wife's record. Two of the children, pava and Paulina, also share 24 December 1895 and are probably one girl twice.

tree: Wife of George Untersinger; mother of Rosalia (1802), Ana (1807), Michael (1810), Lucia (1827) and Eva (1839)
record: Born 25 June 1788, died 1828 — fourteen at the first birth and eleven years dead at the last
why: The five children span thirty-seven years across a mother who lived forty. Both ends break: Rosalia arrives when Helena is fourteen, Eva eleven years after she is buried. This is the same shape as Vladimira Baricevic's row — one marriage record holding two generations of mothers — and it is the commonest way this tree goes wrong. Untersinger is a married-in line and belongs to the Defranceski archive.

tree: Husband of Marija Žabkar; father of five children born 1938–1968
record: Born 11 April 1894 and died 27 March 1896, aged twenty-three months
why: He is a baby who did not reach two, carrying a wife and five children born forty years after his funeral. A later Ivan — named after him, as the custom was — has had his family attached to the child who died. His parents are Josephus de Franceschi and Anica Kalanj of Crikvenica, so the join matters to the Kalanj work here as well as to the Defranceski archive.

tree: Father of Antonija Butkovic (1880–1891)
record: Born 1872 — eight years old at her birth
why: Antonija carries his surname and dies at eleven. She is his sister, not his daughter: their parents are Ivan Butković and Ana Blažević, and the tree already has that couple. A sibling recorded as a child is the second-commonest join error in this tree after the two-generation spouse slot.

tree: Father of Margaretha Jankovic (1757) and Magdalena (1768)
record: Died 10 December 1755 — nineteen months before the first birth
why: His widow Jelena Janković lived to 1805, fifty years after him, and the elder child carries Jelena's surname rather than his. These are the children of her second marriage, attached to her first husband. The register is not needed to see it: the surname on the daughter says whose household she was born into.

tree: Mother of ante Boras (1931–1967)
record: Born 11 June 1922 — nine years old at his birth
why: Her husband Pavao Boras was nineteen in 1931, which is possible; she was nine, which is not. The mother link is the wrong one. Note also that Pavao is recorded dead on 16 December 1940 and Ladislava on 16 December 1942 — the same day two years apart, which is the sort of coincidence that usually turns out to be a copied field.

tree: Father of Lucas Ugrin Adamich (1822), Catharina (1834) and Antonia (1836)
record: Born 30 August 1813 — nine years old at the first birth
why: His wife Magdalena Žubrinić was born 1812 and would have been ten. Lucas is twelve years clear of the other two children and is the one that breaks; Catharina and Antonia sit comfortably. This one is answerable from a book: the Otočac baptisms are filmed from 1834, so Catharina's and Antonia's own entries will name their parents and settle whether Lucas belongs to this couple or to the generation above.

tree: Father of Mattheus «Matolin» di Franceschi (1794) and Lucia (1820)
record: Born 13 April 1785, married 1812 at Gračišće — nine years old at Mattheus's birth
why: Mattheus is born eighteen years before the marriage he is filed under. Lucia, born 1820, fits it exactly. Since Matolin is the name the Defranceski line runs through, this is a join that archive will want to cut rather than this one.

tree: Mother of Giuseppe Defranceschi (4 March 1765), Franciscus (1785) and Giovanni Battista (1787)
record: Born 1753 — twelve years old at Giuseppe's birth
why: Giuseppe's 1765 sits twenty years before his two brothers and breaks both parents at once: Teresa would be twelve and Johannes fifteen. Either the year is mis-keyed or Giuseppe belongs to the generation above. The two 1780s births are unremarkable.

what: The same fact, seen from the father
tree: Father of Giuseppe Defranceschi at fifteen
record: One outlying child, not two bad joins
why: This row and Teresa Grach's are raised by a single date — Giuseppe's 4 March 1765 — reported once against each parent. Fifteen is not impossible for a father, so on its own it would be a doubt rather than a finding; it is the mother at twelve that makes the date untenable. Settling Giuseppe settles both rows.

tree: Georgius Prpic born 26 March 1962, son of Maria Šojat
record: She died in 1891 at Krivi Put 136, aged 67–68
why: A mother of 139 is a four-digit year with a slip in it, not a finding about the past. His brothers arrive 1858, 1862 and 1865, so an 18-- year in that decade is what is meant. This one is reachable: Krivi Put baptisms are filmed 1847–1884 and his entry is inside them.

tree: Married 16 February 1835
record: Born 22 January 1896
why: Sixty-one years before his own birth. The day and month will be right and the century is not: 1935 is the reading that makes the rest of the record work. Gologorica, so the Defranceski archive's line rather than this one.

tree: Married 1868 at Senj
record: Born 1868
why: Married in the year of her birth. Only one of the two marriages the tree gives her carries a date, and it is her birth year repeated into the marriage field — the plainest kind of transcription slip, and the only one here that needs no reasoning at all.

tree: Mother of Ivana Jovanovic (1881–1943)
record: Born 1868 — thirteen years old at the birth
why: Her husband Ranisav was twenty. Thirteen is below what this archive will accept without a document, and no document exists here: this branch is at Gornja Grabovica and Blizonje in Serbia, outside every parish and film this archive can reach. It is recorded as doubtful and left there.

what: Age at her eldest son's birth
tree: Josip Petar Defranceski born 3 December 1911; she was born 28 February 1895
record: Sixteen, and six months before the marriage of 21 June 1912
why: Sixteen with a first child six months before the wedding is unusual and entirely possible, and a marriage following the birth is a pattern this archive meets often. Nothing here contradicts anything. It is flagged only because the check counts every parent under seventeen. Her fifth son is Ivan Anton Defranceski, 1925–1995, whose stone stands at Senj.

tree: Rosalia Untersinger born 1802; he was born 25 March 1787
record: Fifteen — improbable, not impossible
why: The real problem in this family is his wife Helena's, and it is recorded against her: five children across thirty-seven years and eleven of them after she died. His own row is only the father's half of Rosalia's date. A father of fifteen would be remarkable; a mother of fourteen is the one to doubt.

tree: Mother of Vladimira Boras (born 2 January 1960)
record: Born 1904 — fifty-six at the birth, thirty-seven years after her first child
why: Her nine other children run 1923 to 1946. A tenth in 1960 is a grandchild recorded a generation too high, which is the mirror image of the sibling-as-child error. The same family record also carries Domagoj Boras as born 21 October 1946 and dead the previous August, so at least two of its dates are unsafe. Her father is Fabo Milković — worth noting beside the Senj stone this archive first read as «Pavo» Boras and corrected to Fabo: the name is real in this circle.

tree: Died after 1926; son Bruno born 5 August 1939
record: «AFT 1926» is an open bound, not a date
why: A hedge is doing exactly what a hedge is for: it says the death is somewhere after 1926 and names no year. A son in 1939 is inside that. The check raises it because it compares a bound with a firm date, and /impossible already files this class as «not an error at all». It is written down here so the count of unanswered rows can go to nought without pretending anything was found.

what: Not a contradiction, and a bucket in the tree
tree: Born before 1750; son Johanes born 22 July 1762
record: «BEF 1750» is an open bound in the other direction
why: Born before 1750 means any year up to it, so a son in 1762 says nothing. The row worth keeping from this record is a different one: his father is entered in the tree as «Grah's for Investigation (not real)» — a sorting bucket carrying a person's number. This archive already audits the tree for buckets, and that audit did not have this one: its phrase list was written from the buckets that were causing trouble, so it knew «for sorting» and «to be sorted» and «it seems» and not «PLACEHOLDER», «for Investigation» or «(not real)». Five were missing, parenting thirty-six people between them. None of the thirty-six is published, so no count on this site was ever wrong — which is why it went unnoticed, and is the reason to fix it rather than not to. A detector written from the examples in front of it will always be shaped like those examples.

tree: Wife of Michael Žubrinić; mother of six children, 1822 to 1844
record: Born 14 March 1793, died 1831 — the last three children arrive after her death
why: Her first three — Franciscus 1822, Michael 1825, Josephus 1828 — sit exactly where a woman born in 1793 should have them. Stephanus 1833, Josephus 1836 and Theresia 1844 are all after she is buried, and the second Josephus repeats a name already in use, which a household does not do while the first is alive. Michael remarried and the second wife's children have been put on the first. Which Michael is a separate question and a harder one: the house numbers say he is at least seven men.

tree: Wife of Phillipus Žubrinić; mother of eight children, 1828 to 1847
record: Born 13 January 1809, died 1845 — and Phillipus died in 1845 too
why: Seven of the eight children run 1828 to 1843 without a quarrel. Only Magdalena, 9 May 1847, breaks, and she breaks against both parents at once, because husband and wife are recorded dead in the same year. A child born two years after a household ends is a grandchild or a niece filed a generation too high. The couple dying together in 1845 is worth a question of its own — this archive already holds one epidemic year in these parishes — but the tree gives no cause and none is assumed here.

tree: Mother of eight, the last Joannes in 1844
record: Born 5 August 1784 at Prozor 50; her husband Josephus died in 1825
why: Seven children run 1806 to 1826 — the last of them the year after Josephus dies, which is ordinary. Joannes in 1844 is nineteen years past his father's death and puts his mother at sixty. He is a grandson recorded as a son. The useful detail is the address: she is born at Prozor 50, one of the seven houses that separate the Michael Žubrinići, so this household can be pinned to a door rather than to a name.

tree: Born 1809; mother of four Kraljić children, 1807 to 1820
record: The eldest is born 29 September 1807, two years before she is
why: The four children are unremarkable together: 1807, 1812, 1817, 1820 is an ordinary sibling span. It is the mother's single year that disagrees with all four, so the error is one field and not four joins — and 1809 is the sort of number that gets written into a birth when it belongs to a marriage. Her husband Jacobi Kraljić has no dates at all, so nothing else in the record pushes back.

tree: Mother of five, the last Martha in 1861
record: Born 1810 — fifty-one at Martha's birth, and eleven years older than her husband
why: Her first four arrive 1848, 1851, 1853, 1854, then nothing for seven years. Fifty-one is improbable rather than impossible, so this is recorded as doubtful and not as a finding. It also cannot be settled the usual way: the Otočac baptisms are filmed from 1834 to 1858 and Martha's 1861 falls outside the film. The eleven-year gap to Joannes, born 1821, is the second oddity and may be the same error seen twice.

what: Not a contradiction — an estimate against a firm date
tree: Mother of Anton Martin «Tone» Blažević, born about 1840; she was born 13 March 1825
record: She married Anton Kljapo Blažević on 28 August 1842 at Krivi Put
why: Her eight other children run 1852 to 1865 and none of them raises anything. The one that does is «ABT 1840» — a hedged year, two years before a marriage that is recorded to the day. An estimate is not evidence against a date, so nothing here contradicts anything: either Tone's year is simply wrong, or he is his father's son by an earlier mother. The check misses the hedge because the hedge is on the child and it only looks at the person it is reporting — a narrow gap, and the only one this sweep found in the tool itself.
